title: CompiledProblemMetadata
description: The serializable metadata of a compiled problem (plan §2.1, §2.2 P02/K01 row; frozen in docs/interfaces-frozen.md §1). Executable objects stay runtime-local: only this travels. Promoted by K01, which is the window ADR 0008 D4.1 and D4.4 name for adding `parameter_ids` and `row_accumulation` — adding either later would be a migration. Four rules a JSON Schema cannot express are checked by tests/test_k01_schemas.py: `row_accumulation` must key exactly `equation_ids`; `variable_ids`, `equation_ids` and `parameter_ids` must each be unique; every `column_scales` key must be a variable and every `row_scales` key an equation; and a scale must be finite and strictly positive, because a scale divides.

model_version.description: Identifies equation structure and backend form only, never pinned-input values (ADR 0008 D4.1). Two instances differing solely in specification values share this. Format `<label>@<structure_sha256>` (ADR 0002 D2.3): the label names the function family and the 64 hex characters are the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the structure document — variable_ids, equation_ids, parameter_ids and row_accumulation. The compiler assigns it; a reader recomputes it where the document carries those lists.

backend_version.description: Exact version. The [A10] audit in docs/p03-binary-audit.md is of these bytes.

variable_ids.description: The ordered free variables. `x` is dense in this order.

parameter_ids.description: The order `constants_sha256` hashes the complete pinned-input vector in — physical constants, model parameters and specification values (ADR 0008 D4.1). May be empty only for a problem with no pinned inputs at all.

column_scales.description: By variable id. A scale divides, so it is strictly positive.

row_accumulation.description: How each row's conservation content accumulates, by equation id, copied from the contributing manifests (ADR 0008 D4.4). T04 reads this to place the nonzero entries of the PTC mass matrix `M`, so a guessed entry here becomes a wrong `M` there rather than a visible error.

accumulation.description: ADR 0008 D3. `absent` is for a row whose accumulation genuinely cannot be known — one produced by an opaque evaluator. A row the compiler itself authors, such as a tear or a specification-promotion row, is `algebraic`, because the compiler wrote it and knows.

capabilities.description: Negotiated optional capabilities. Every field is required and none has a default: a default would let a backend that declares nothing be read as having declared something. A missing exact Hessian is `absent`, never zeros.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 under the canonical encoding of process_runtime.canonical.
